name: cx-goal-one-rule
task: Open the door and then pick up the box in the other room, and try not to drop the key while the door is still closed.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: The task commands opening the door, but the clauses only require it as a prerequisite to picking up the box; the environment makes that prerequisite happen, yet the task also requires the stated order. Add hard Precedence(blocker_moved, door_open) and Precedence(has_door_key, door_open) only if those prerequisites are stated? They are not stated, so do not add them. The required hard Existence(target_picked_up) with Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up) already forces door_open, and no separate Existence(door_open) is needed. However, the soft Absence(key_lost) misrepresents “try not to drop the key while the door is still closed”: key_lost is only an event when the key is lost while the door is closed, so this correctly captures that preference. No changes needed.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The task commands opening the door, but no clause makes `door_open` happen; `Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up)` only orders it before the box. Add a hard `Existence(door_open)`. The soft `Absence(key_lost)` correctly captures “try not to drop the key while the door is still closed.”

CHANGES REQUIRED: the hard Existence(target_picked_up) repeats what it already requires alongside hard Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up), which forces door_open before the required pickup. Remove the redundant Existence clause. Keep the hard Precedence and soft Absence(key_lost).

CHANGES REQUIRED: The task commands opening the door and picking up the box, but the clauses only impose an order; neither event is required. Add hard Existence(target_picked_up) alongside Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up), which also forces door_open. The soft Absence(key_lost) correctly captures “try not to drop the key while the door is still closed.”

CHANGES REQUIRED: The task commands opening the door and then picking up the box, but the clauses contain only Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up), which requires neither event. Add hard Existence(target_picked_up); with the hard Precedence, this also forces door_open. Keep the soft Absence(key_lost), which matches “try not to drop the key while the door is still closed.”

NO CHANGES NEEDED: Existence(target_picked_up) and Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up) require the box and its order after opening the door. Soft Absence(key_lost) correctly captures the preference not to drop the key while the door is closed.

texts: Pick up the box in the other room after opening the door.
Open the door before picking up the box in the other room.
Prefer not to lose the key while the door is still closed.
